transport: RJ45 RS-485 to Bluetooth 5.0 / BLE (compatible with 4.0) · serial side 2400–115200 bps, default 115200 · powered 5 V ±0.5 V from the RS-485 comms port, 5 V @ 30 mA · one adapter serves exactly one controller, inverter or inverter/charger (one-to-one only)
sharedMapEvidence: NOT A DIALECT, and unreachable as recorded. It has no register map of its own; it fronts whatever is on the RJ45. The far-end map is the controller's. But unlike the USB cable, the near side is a BLE link whose service UUIDs, characteristic UUIDs, and frame layout are stated in NO document found — vendor or community — so there is currently no route from a Linux gateway to the controller through i
gotchas: THE BLOCKING FACT: no EPEver document gives a GATT service UUID, a characteristic UUID, an advertisement layout, or a frame format for this adapter. The only statement the manual makes about the wire is the bullet 'Support data encryption', which is not a specification. Compare Victron, which publishes a record-layout

No community implementation was found either. Searches for a decoder, a GATT dump, or a Python client for the EPEver BLE RJ45 adapters returned nothing but reprints of the same user manual. That is a hard `unverified` — not one weak source, zero sources.

The vendor manual contradicts itself on range inside one revision (V1.2): the Features list says 'Up to 30 meters communication distance', the specification table says '≤ 10m', and the step-4 note says 'The phone and the Bluetooth module can't be placed more than 10 meters away.' Recorded, not resolved. If range matter
One-to-one, and it occupies the controller's only RJ45 port. It cannot coexist with the USB-RS485 cable on the same port, and the MT50 bus-contention note in docs/INVENTORY.md applies unchanged.

The A manual publishes NO RJ45 pin definition. The BLE RJ45 D manual does (1,2 = +5VDC · 3,4 = RS485-B · 5,6 = RS485-A · 7,8 = GND — the same pinout docs/DEVICES.md already records from the IPower-Plus manual). Do not carry D's pinout onto A. Ring it out with a meter, as docs/HARDWARE.md already instructs.
